title: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Energy Transfer
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Biology: Photosynthesis and Respiration Worksheets
standard_code: A level Biology: Energy transfers in and between organisms
standard_text: Light-dependent and light-independent reactions of photosynthesis, limiting factors, glycolysis, the link reaction, the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, anaerobic respiration, respiratory quotient, energy transfer through ecosystems, productivity and nutrient cycles.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level biology worksheets on energy transfers: photosynthesis, respiration, Rf values, respiratory quotient, GPP and NPP, efficiency, and the nitrogen cycle. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Efficiency = energy at next level ÷ energy at previous level × 100.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis: the light-dependent reaction on the thylakoids uses light to make ATP and reduced NADP and splits water (photolysis); the Calvin cycle in the stroma fixes CO₂ with rubisco. Respiration: glycolysis (cytoplasm), link reaction and Krebs cycle (matrix) and oxidative phosphorylation (cristae).

Net primary production NPP = GPP − respiratory losses. Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level. RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in (1.0 for carbohydrate, 0.7 for lipid).

Example

GPP 20,000, R 12,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. NPP?

20,000 − 12,000

Answer: 8,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹

Example

O₂ in 30 cm³, CO₂ out 21 cm³. RQ?

21 ÷ 30

Answer: 0.7

Common mistakes

  • Adding respiration to GPP to get NPP.
  • Dividing O₂ by CO₂ for RQ.
  • Putting glycolysis in the mitochondria.

faq.q: What is the difference between GPP and NPP?
faq.a: GPP is the total chemical energy made by photosynthesis; NPP is what is left after the plant's own respiration.

faq.q: Why does anaerobic respiration make so little ATP?
faq.a: Without oxygen the electron transfer chain and Krebs cycle stop, so only glycolysis makes ATP.

items.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis fall at very high temperatures?
c: enzymes such as rubisco are denatured
items.e: Stomata may also close.

In a chromatogram of leaf pigments, a pigment spot moves 2.4 cm and the solvent moves 8.0 cm. Calculate its R<sub>f</sub> value.
What happens to glycerate 3-phosphate (GP) in the Calvin cycle?
c: it is reduced to triose phosphate using ATP and reduced NADP
items.e: Some triose phosphate makes glucose; most regenerates RuBP.

items.q: How is ATP made in the light-dependent reaction?
c: protons flow through ATP synthase down a gradient (chemiosmosis)
items.e: This is photophosphorylation.

items.q: What happens to RuBP if the CO₂ concentration falls?
c: it builds up, because less is being used
items.e: GP falls at the same time.

What is the role of NADP in photosynthesis?
c: it accepts electrons and protons, becoming reduced NADP
items.e: Reduced NADP is used to reduce GP.

items.q: Why do growers burn paraffin in greenhouses?
c: it raises CO₂ concentration and temperature
items.e: Both can limit photosynthesis.

What is photolysis?

items.e: 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ + O₂.

items.q: What does chlorophyll absorb mainly?

items.e: CO₂ + RuBP → 2 GP.

items.q: Where does the Calvin cycle (light-independent reaction) take place?

An organism takes in 36 cm³ of oxygen and gives out 32 cm³ of carbon dioxide. Calculate the respiratory quotient.
items.e: RQ = CO₂ given out ÷ O₂ taken in = 0.889 (1.0 for carbohydrate, about 0.7 for lipid, about 0.9 for protein).

items.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in mammals?
items.e: Pyruvate is reduced, regenerating NAD.

items.q: Where does the Krebs cycle take place?
items.e: Acetyl CoA joins oxaloacetate.

items.q: Why does anaerobic respiration make much less ATP?
c: only glycolysis produces ATP; the Krebs cycle and electron transfer chain stop
items.e: Only 2 ATP per glucose.

items.q: How many ATP molecules are made directly in one turn of the Krebs cycle?
items.e: Two turns per glucose give two ATP.

items.q: The producers contain 12,000 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹ and the primary consumers contain 2,400 kJ m⁻² year⁻¹. Calculate the efficiency of energy transfer.

items.q: What is denitrification?
c: bacteria convert nitrates into nitrogen gas in waterlogged soil
items.e: It happens in anaerobic conditions.

items.q: Why do intensive farming methods keep animals warm and still?
c: less energy is lost in respiration, so more goes into growth
items.e: This improves efficiency of energy transfer.

items.q: What is the main reason energy is lost between trophic levels?

items.q: What is eutrophication?
c: excess nutrients cause algal growth, leading to low oxygen levels in water
items.e: Bacteria decomposing dead algae use up oxygen.

items.q: What is net production in a consumer?

nitrates are converted to nitrogen gas

items.q: What are mycorrhizae?

items.e: The plant gives the fungus sugars.

items.q: Why is phosphate needed by plants?

items.e: Phosphate comes from rocks, not the air.
